simple.meaning: פְּלָיָה (Pᵉlâyâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “Pelajah , the name of three Israelites.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פְּלָיָה (H6411) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Chronicles 3:24, with occurrences in 1 Chronicles, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פְּלָיָה (H6411) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פְּלָיָה (H6411) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פְּלָיָה (Pᵉlâyâh) / H6411 is traced through 1 Chronicles 3:24, Nehemiah 8:7, Nehemiah 10:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Pelajah , the name of three Israelites
definitions.full: H6411. Pelayah מְּלָאיָה proper name, masculine Neh 8:7 ; 10:11 , ᵐ5 L Φαλαιας . מְּלָיָה proper name, masculine (late Assyrian Pi-lîâma Hilpr Univ. Pa. Exp. ix. 68 ); — 1Chr 3:24 , Φαρα , Φαλαια , Φαδια .
definitions.rootNote: or פְּלָאיָה ; from 6381 and 3050 ; Jah has distinguished ;

occurrences.englishText: The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven.

Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law; and the people stayed in their place.
